newsitem.title: LEBANON: Saudi will shun Mideast economic conference.
newsitem.headline: Saudi will shun Mideast economic conference.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Abdullah in remarks published on Monday said the kingdom would not attend a controversial Arab-Israeli economic conference in Doha in November and that Riyadh had advised Qatar to cancel it.
"We told them this conference will harm them and we advised them that we and most Arabs (states) will not attend," he told as-Safir newspaper while on a visit to Lebanon which ended on Saturday.
"We advised them (Qatari leaders) to drop this conference...," he added.

Qatar, which is due to host the fourth economic conference since landmark Middle East peace negotiations began in 1991, has said it is committed to holding the gathering but has come under pressure from some Arab countries.

Arab states have expressed anger over Israel's policies on peace. Talks between the Palestinians and Israel collapsed in March after the Jewish state began to build a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil producer, is an influential player in the Middle East and a key United States ally. It attended the three previous meetings.
The Saudi Crown Prince told as-Safir that the United States had asked Saudi Arabia to attend the Doha conference.
"We informed them of our viewpoint. How can this happen when Jerusalem is being lost and swallowed? There is no way we can forget Jerusalem," he said.
Prince Abdullah added that he urged Qatari leaders to make Arab interests a priority.
"They informed us that they are under strong pressure to hold it (the conference) in Doha," he said.

"So we said you must inform whoever is pressuring you that you have counter pressure from the Arabs...The emir of Qatar is kind. And we were hoping that he would meet the requests of his brothers...," Prince Abdullah told as-Safir.
An Arab League official said on Sunday most Arab countries opposed attending the conference because of Israel's policies.

Mohammed Zakariya Ismail, its assistant secretary general for political affairs, also told reporters the United States should play a more active role in persuading Israel to respect the principles of the peace process.

Syria last week indirectly criticised Qatar for planning to host the gathering in which Israel is scheduled to take part, saying Arabs should give priority to commitments they made to each other rather than to commitments made to Israel.
